tools.name: ableton_status
tools.summary: Connection state, Set summary and finding counts.
tools.description: Call this first in a session, and whenever the user asks what is in the Set or whether Live is connected. Returns tempo, time signature, track and scene counts, whether transport is running, and how the material is split between Arrangement and Session. Also refreshes the snapshot every other read answers from.

tools.name: ableton_guide
tools.summary: The command sheet for the current mode.
tools.description: Lists the tools available in this session with a one-line description each, plus the producer-language examples they accept. Use it when the user asks what Enableton can do.

mode.description: Mode to describe; defaults to the current one.

tools.name: ableton_escalate
tools.summary: Compile a bounded plan from current findings when a mode needs a fix outside it.
tools.description: Compiles up to 12 steps across 3 phases from the current Set's findings. Intent is matched against finding titles, kinds, phases and locations; an explicit context.finding_ids or context.phases selects precisely. The compiler never invents tool arguments: an intent with no matching finding returns no plan and a reason. The plan is stored and expires after 10 minutes; it does not write Live. Call ableton_plan_apply with the returned plan_id to execute it.
examples: fix the gain issue outside this mode

intent.description: What the caller is trying to fix.

tools.name: ableton_plan_apply
tools.summary: Apply a stored escalation plan transactionally.
tools.description: Loads the plan by plan_id and applies its steps through the transactional executor: preflight every step, make a scratch copy, apply top to bottom, stop at the first failure and restore exactly. A successful apply deletes the plan; a failed apply keeps it for inspection. Plans expire after 10 minutes. This writes Live; use ableton_escalate or inspect_plan first to inspect the steps.

tools.name: ableton_plan_discard
tools.summary: Discard a stored escalation plan.
tools.description: Deletes a plan by plan_id without touching Live. A plan that is already gone returns discarded false; it does not fabricate success.

tools.name: ableton_undo
tools.summary: Undo the last transaction Enableton applied.
tools.description: Restores the last transaction this server applied, from the restore tokens the tools themselves returned. Live's own undo is linear and cannot unwind a plan; this consumes Enableton's record instead. The record holds one applied write and expires after 10 minutes. It is refused when nothing was applied, when the record expired, or when the current Set is not the Set the transaction was applied to. Restores replay in reverse, and the record is cleared afterwards, so a partial undo is reported and never replayed twice.

scope.description: Only the last transaction is supported in this build.

tools.name: inspect_structure
tools.summary: How the Set is built: sections, tracks, clips and device counts.
tools.description: Derives sections from where arrangement clips actually are, because these Sets have no named locators. Returns the bar count, the sections with their clip and track counts, per-track rows with clip and device counts, and the signals worth knowing first: duplicate track names, how many sections are named, and the Arrangement versus Session split.

tools.name: inspect_unused
tools.summary: Material doing nothing: empty tracks, empty scenes, ambiguous names.
tools.description: Names the tracks with no clips anywhere, the scenes with nothing in them, the tracks with no devices, empty Session slots, and any names shared by more than one track. It does not claim clips were never launched: that is not observable, and a guess would be worse than silence.
examples: find dead weight in this set

tools.name: mix_levels_report
tools.summary: Every fader, pan and mute, with the outliers flagged.
tools.description: Returns volume and pan per track with Live's own display string where available, plus flags for muted, soloed, at-unity and silent tracks and any duplicate names. Peak levels are reported as not measured rather than estimated; measuring them needs a meter pass.

tools.name: mix_headroom
tools.summary: Fader trim, and the headroom that still needs meter data.
tools.description: Reports each track's fader in Live's own dB display, with flags for fader trim above unity, at unity, below unity, silent, muted and soloed. It does not derive a headroom number from faders: peak data is not in the snapshot, so true headroom is reported as unmeasured and mix_meter_poll is named as the missing capability. The master fader is likewise reported unavailable because the snapshot carries only the master device chain.
examples: how much headroom do I have

tools.name: notes_overlaps
tools.summary: Same-pitch MIDI notes whose time ranges collide.
tools.description: Checks every MIDI clip in the Arrangement and Session for notes of the same pitch whose time ranges intersect, and returns each collision pair with both positions and the overlap length. Chords are not flagged. The snapshot carries only bounded collision pairs; if capture was truncated or a clip's notes could not be read, the result says so and marks itself incomplete instead of claiming zero overlaps. A snapshot from before note capture reports unavailable with the required script version.

tools.name: notes_read
tools.summary: Read one MIDI clip's notes, with source and paging.
tools.description: Resolves one MIDI clip by exact track and clip name, optionally constrained by location and session slot, then returns its notes in time order with pitch, start, duration, velocity and mute. Duplicate matches are refused rather than guessed. Reads through get_all_notes_extended when Live exposes it and the legacy notes vector otherwise; the source that answered travels with the result. A non-MIDI clip or an unreadable note vector reports notes_available false with the reason instead of an empty list. Paging is by note, not by clip.
examples: read the notes in this clip
what notes are in the bass clip

track.description: Exact track name; duplicates are rejected.

tools.name: notes_quantize
tools.summary: Move note starts toward a grid, with strength and exact restore.
tools.description: Quantizes each note's start to the nearest grid line in beats, with strength blending from 0 (unchanged) to 1 (full snap). Durations, pitches and velocities are untouched. Dry-run by default; applying returns an undo token holding the clip's original note vector, and restore writes that vector back exactly. Ties at half a grid step move later.

grid.description: Grid step in beats; 0.25 is a sixteenth in 4/4.

tools.name: notes_transform
tools.summary: Transpose, rescale velocity or stretch note durations.
tools.description: Applies pitch, velocity and duration changes to every note without changing their starts or the note count. Transposition refuses rather than clipping a pitch outside 0-127; velocity is clamped to 0-127. At least one transform must be given. Dry-run by default; applying returns an undo token holding the original vector, and restore writes it back exactly.
examples: transpose this clip up a fifth

tools.name: notes_humanize
tools.summary: Add seeded timing and velocity variation.
tools.description: Moves each note start by a random offset within the timing window and each velocity within the velocity window. The seed makes the result reproducible: the same clip and seed produce the same variation. Starts never go below zero and velocities stay within 0-127. Dry-run by default; applying returns an undo token holding the original vector, and restore writes it back exactly.
examples: loosen this pattern without changing the notes

tools.name: notes_strum
tools.summary: Stagger chord notes in pitch order.
tools.description: Groups notes that share a start and delays them in pitch order: up starts the lowest note first, down starts the highest first. Notes outside a chord are untouched. Dry-run by default; applying returns an undo token holding the original vector, and restore writes it back exactly.

tools.name: notes_replace
tools.summary: Replace a clip's whole note vector.
tools.description: Replaces every note in one MIDI clip with the supplied list; an empty list clears the clip. Each note needs pitch, start and duration, with optional velocity and mute. This is the primitive for generated or imported patterns. Dry-run by default; applying returns an undo token holding the original vector, and restore writes it back exactly.
examples: replace this clip with these notes
write this pattern into the clip
clear the notes in this clip

tools.name: notes_scale_lock
tools.summary: Move out-of-scale pitches to the nearest scale tone.
tools.description: Constrains pitches to a named scale from a named root, moving each out-of-scale note to the nearest pitch in the scale; ties move down. Starts, durations, velocities and note count are unchanged. Dry-run by default; applying returns an undo token holding the original vector, and restore writes it back exactly.
examples: lock this bass to C minor
put these notes in F# major

root.description: Pitch class 0-11 or a note name such as C, F# or Eb.

tools.name: clips_warp_check
tools.summary: Warp state for every audio clip, with unreadable or empty data flagged.
tools.description: Checks every audio clip, in the Arrangement and in Session, against the snapshot's warp state: whether Warp is on, the warp mode, the marker count, and whether the marker vector could be read. Returns per-clip rows with flags for unreadable markers, zero markers and unknown modes, plus counts by flag and mode. Warping off is counted rather than flagged, and it does not judge whether a mode suits the material or whether markers sit on the grid; the snapshot carries counts, not positions.
examples: which clips have bad warp data

tools.name: inspect_run
tools.summary: Findings for the current Set with counts per mode.
tools.description: Runs the diagnostic detectors against the snapshot and returns stable findings plus total, per-mode, per-severity, needs-listening and auto-fixable counts. Tiers are fast (hygiene), standard (the default: hygiene, gain and notes) and deep. The notes detector reports only overlaps present in the snapshot; missing note data is returned as unavailable with its reason, never as a clean result.

tools.name: inspect_report
tools.summary: Filter and page the current Set's findings.
tools.description: Returns the full finding counts plus a filtered, paged list. Filters are mode, severity, phase and needs_listening; an empty filtered list is distinct from a Set with no findings because the unfiltered counts remain visible.

tools.name: inspect_finding
tools.summary: Read one finding by its stable id.
tools.description: Returns one finding with its evidence, location, phase, mode, severity, confidence and either a concrete fix or needs_listening. An unknown id is an error, not an empty result.

tools.name: inspect_plan
tools.summary: Build a bounded, phase-ordered repair plan without writing.
tools.description: Turns available findings into plan steps, ordered grid to master and capped at 12 steps across 3 phases. Findings that need listening are listed but never become steps; a fix whose tool is missing or has no dry-run is returned as unavailable with the reason. Truncation is reported explicitly.

tools.name: inspect_autofix
tools.summary: Apply available fixes phase by phase, with count checks and rollback.
tools.description: Dry-run by default. Applying runs one phase at a time through the transactional executor, re-reads after each phase, and stops as soon as the total finding count rises above the starting count. needs_listening findings are never applied, and an error-severity finding blocks the rest of its phase.

tools.name: clips_duplicate_range
tools.summary: Duplicate arrangement clips from one bar range to another.
tools.description: Copies every arrangement clip whose start falls in the half-open bar range [from_bar, to_bar) on the selected tracks, preserving its offset from the range start. Dry-run by default and returns the predicted destination for each clip. Applying is one transactional write; the returned undo token deletes exactly the clips it created.

tracks.description: Track names; omit for all tracks.

restore.description: Internal rollback token returned by an applied duplicate.

tools.name: tracks_list
tools.summary: List tracks with name, colour, volume, pan and sends.
tools.description: Returns a page of tracks in Set order with Live's mixer state and return-send levels. Colour is a packed 24-bit RGB integer (0xRRGGBB). Use offset/limit for large Sets; next_offset is null on the last page.

tools.name: tracks_set_volume
tools.summary: Set a track fader, with dry-run and exact restore.
tools.description: Sets the volume of the named tracks (or all tracks when omitted). Volume is 0..1 as Live stores it, so 0.85 is 0.0 dB. Dry-run by default; applying returns one undo token per track and restore puts back exactly those values.

tools.name: tracks_gain_stage
tools.summary: Normalise track levels toward a headroom target.
tools.description: Moves each track's volume so its observed peak sits headroom_db below full scale. Tracks without a measured peak are skipped and named in the result. Dry-run by default.
examples: even out all the track levels

restore.description: Internal rollback token returned by an applied gain stage.

tools.name: devices_read_chain
tools.summary: Read a track's device chain, including nested rack chains.
tools.description: Reads one track's device tree from the cached snapshot. Devices inside racks stay nested under each device's chains field; the result also gives the top-level count and recursive total. A track name must identify exactly one track, because a duplicate name is ambiguous and is refused rather than guessed. This does not read parameters or presets.
examples: what is on the drum bus
show me the bass device chain

track.description: Exact track name; duplicates are rejected.

tools.name: master_chain_read
tools.summary: Read the master device chain.
tools.description: Returns the devices on Live's master track, including nested rack chains, plus the recursive device count. When the snapshot could not read the master chain, available is false and the reason is returned instead of an empty chain that looks like a clean master.

tools.name: sections_map
tools.summary: Map the arrangement's occupied sections.
tools.description: Builds sections from contiguous runs of bars that hold arrangement clips. The source field makes clear these are derived from density, not named locators; named_sections counts locators that actually carry names. Use inspect_structure when the full track and signal summary is needed.
examples: where are the sections in this arrangement

tools.name: transport_play
tools.summary: Start playback, optionally from a bar.
tools.description: Starts the transport so the user can hear an edit. Not a performance tool: use it to audition, not to run a set.

from_bar.description: Bar to start from; omit to continue from the playhead.

tools.name: transport_stop
tools.summary: Stop the transport.
tools.description: Stops playback without moving the playhead. It is a direct transport action, not a plan, and is reversible by calling transport_play again. No arguments are accepted.

tools.name: transport_locate
tools.summary: Move the playhead to a bar without starting playback.
tools.description: Locates to a whole or fractional bar using the Set's time signature. It only moves the playhead; use transport_play to start auditioning. The position is in beats and is returned so the caller can inspect it.
examples: put the playhead at the drop

tools.name: transport_set_loop
tools.summary: Set or clear the transport loop range.
tools.description: Turns the loop on or off. When start_bar and end_bar are present they are set together and end_bar must be after start_bar. With no bounds, the existing range is kept and only the enabled flag changes. The result reports the resulting loop state.

tools.name: inspect_export
tools.summary: Export the diagnostic findings to JSON.
tools.description: Runs the requested diagnostic tier and writes the complete findings document to an atomic .json file. The path is optional; without one the export goes under %APPDATA%\Enableton\exports with a UTC timestamp. This does not edit the Live Set, and it refuses a path that is not a .json file.
examples: save the findings to a file

path.description: Destination ending in .json; omitted uses the exports directory.

tools.name: tracks_set_pan
tools.summary: Set track pan positions, with dry-run and exact restore.
tools.description: Sets pan from -1 (left) to 1 (right) for the named tracks, or all tracks when omitted. Dry-run by default; applying returns one undo token per track, and restore puts back exactly those values. Pan is read through the mixer parameter when Live exposes it.

tools.name: tracks_set_sends
tools.summary: Set return-send levels on one track, with dry-run and exact restore.
tools.description: Sets one or more send levels for a named track. Send keys must match return-track names; values are 0..1 as Live stores them. Dry-run by default; applying returns an undo token that restores the exact previous values.
examples: add some reverb to the vocals

tools.name: tracks_name_and_color
tools.summary: Rename or recolour one track, with dry-run and exact restore.
tools.description: Changes a track's name, its colour, or both, resolving the track by name or by Set index (use the index when names are duplicated). Colour is a packed 24-bit RGB integer (0xRRGGBB), as Live reports it; Live snaps a requested RGB to its nearest track colour, so read the track back to see the stored value. Dry-run by default; applying returns an undo token that restores the exact previous name and colour.

track_index.description: Set index; use instead of track when names are duplicated.

tools.name: clips_rename
tools.summary: Rename an arrangement or session clip.
tools.description: Resolves a clip by exact track and clip name, optionally constrained by location and session slot. Duplicate matches are refused rather than guessed. Dry-run by default; applying returns an undo token that restores the previous name.

tools.name: clips_set_warp_mode
tools.summary: Set an audio clip's warp mode, with dry-run and exact restore.
tools.description: Changes one audio clip's warp mode by enum value or name (beats, tones, texture, re-pitch, complex, rex, complex_pro). The clip is resolved by track and clip name, optionally constrained by location and session slot; duplicate matches are refused. MIDI clips are unavailable with a reason. Warp on/off is not changed. Dry-run by default; applying returns an undo token that restores the exact previous mode.
examples: set the vocal clip to complex pro
put this loop back on beats

tools.name: clips_fix_loop_points
tools.summary: Set a clip's loop boundaries, with dry-run and exact restore.
tools.description: Sets a looped MIDI or warped-audio clip's loop start and end in clip-relative beats. Both values are validated against the clip length; unwarped audio uses seconds and is unavailable with a reason, and an unlooped clip is refused because its loop end is its clip end. The clip's looping flag, start/end markers and notes are not changed. Duplicate clip names are refused. Dry-run by default; applying returns an undo token that restores the exact previous loop points.
examples: tighten this loop to whole bars
set the loop points on this clip

loop_start.description: Clip-relative beat for the loop start.

loop_end.description: Clip-relative beat for the loop end.

tools.name: sections_create_locators
tools.summary: Create named locators at bar boundaries, with dry-run and exact restore.
tools.description: Creates one named locator per requested bar. Live has no create-locator call: a cue is toggled at the playhead, and the same call deletes an existing cue. So this tool reads the locator list first and refuses a bar that already holds one instead of silently removing it. The playhead is moved only to the beats being written and is put back afterwards. Dry-run by default; applying returns an undo token that deletes exactly the cues it created.

restore.description: Internal rollback token returned by an applied create.

tools.name: sections_move
tools.summary: Move a locator to another bar, with dry-run and exact restore.
tools.description: Moves one locator, selected by exact bar or unique name, to another bar. Live 12.2.5 has no setter for Locator.time, so a move is a create at the destination followed by a delete at the source. An occupied destination is refused instead of replacing that marker, the locator keeps its name, and the playhead is put back. Dry-run by default; applying returns an undo token that moves the cue back.
examples: move the intro marker to bar 9
shift my drop locator four bars later

bar.description: Bar of the locator to move.

name.description: Unique name of the locator to move.

restore.description: Internal rollback token returned by an applied move.

tools.name: sections_delete
tools.summary: Delete locators by name, bar or all of them, with exact restore.
tools.description: Deletes the locators selected by exact name, by bar, or every locator when all is true. Exactly one selector is required, and a duplicated name is refused rather than guessed. A deleted marker keeps its name and time in the undo token, so restore recreates the cue exactly. Dry-run by default; a bar with no locator is an error, not a silent skip.

restore.description: Internal rollback token returned by an applied delete.

tools.name: sections_scenes_from_sections
tools.summary: Create one Scene per locator, named after it, with dry-run and exact restore.
tools.description: Turns the Set's locators into Session scenes, in time order. A locator with no name is skipped and named in the result; a scene that already carries the name is skipped too, so running this twice does not duplicate scenes. Dry-run by default; applying returns an undo token holding each created scene's index and name, and restore deletes exactly those.

prefix.description: Optional name prefix for every created scene.

restore.description: Internal rollback token returned by an applied create.

tools.name: clips_copy
tools.summary: Copy one clip to another Session slot or arrangement bar, with exact restore.
tools.description: Copies one clip within the same track or onto another track, to a Session slot (session sources) or to an arrangement bar (arrangement sources). Live has no primitive for moving between Session and Arrangement, so that combination is refused with the reason instead of approximated. An occupied destination is refused. Dry-run by default; applying returns an undo token naming the clip it created, and restore deletes exactly that.
examples: duplicate this clip onto the drum bus

slot.description: Zero-based source slot for session clips.

to_track.description: Destination track; defaults to the source track.

restore.description: Internal rollback token returned by an applied copy.

tools.name: clips_transpose
tools.summary: Shift a MIDI clip by semitones, with dry-run and exact note restore.
tools.description: Moves every note in one MIDI clip by the given number of semitones. It refuses rather than clipping a pitch outside 0-127. Starts, durations and velocities are untouched, and audio clips are unavailable with a reason. Dry-run by default; applying returns the clip's whole note vector as the undo token, and restore writes it back exactly.
examples: take this bassline up an octave
transpose the chord clip down a fifth
move this part up two semitones

restore.description: Internal rollback token returned by an applied transpose.

tools.name: clips_clear
tools.summary: Empty a MIDI clip, with dry-run and exact note restore.
tools.description: Removes every note from one MIDI clip, leaving the clip itself and its length in place. An audio clip is unavailable with a reason: clearing it would delete audio this tool cannot put back, so it is not attempted. Dry-run by default; applying returns the whole note vector as the undo token, and restore writes it back exactly.
examples: empty the notes in this pattern

restore.description: Internal rollback token returned by an applied clear.

tools.name: tracks_duplicate
tools.summary: Duplicate a track, with dry-run and exact restore.
tools.description: Duplicates one track in place, count times, and returns the dry run's plan as the applied result so the transaction's preflight trace still matches; the name Live has assigned to a copy stays in the undo token, and an empty name is omitted because Live can return the new track before naming it. The copy carries Live's own content: clips, devices and mixer state. Dry-run by default; restore deletes the created tracks by index in descending order, checking the name when one was recorded.
examples: make three copies of this track

restore.description: Internal rollback token returned by an applied duplicate.

tools.name: tracks_set_routing
tools.summary: Set a track's input or output routing, with dry-run and exact restore.
tools.description: Changes one track's input type, input channel, output type or output channel by Live's own display name or by the zero-based index in the option list Live reports. Use an index when a name is duplicated or a channel has no display name; the error lists every option with its index. Live builds the channel list from the selected type, so when changing both, set the type first in a separate call. Dry-run by default; applying returns the previous names, identifiers and indexes as an undo token, and restore resolves by index first so duplicate entries stay exact.
examples: route this track to the master
send the bass to the drum bus
change the input to Ext. In

restore.description: Internal rollback token returned by an applied routing change.

tools.name: tracks_delete
tools.summary: Delete one track after an explicit confirm; irreversible on this Live build.
tools.description: Deletes the resolved track and checks the track count fell by exactly one and that the following track moved into the freed index. This build cannot put a track back: insert_device arrives in Live 12.3, so the delete has no undo token and is declared irreversible. An apply therefore refuses without confirm: true, a dry run reports what the track holds and states that confirmation is required, and a Set with a single track is refused because Live needs at least one.

track.description: Exact track name; duplicates are rejected.

confirm.description: Must be true to apply; this cannot be undone.

tools.name: tracks_clean_empty
tools.summary: Delete empty tracks after an explicit confirm; irreversible on this Live build.
tools.description: Finds tracks with no Arrangement clips and no Session clips, or checks the tracks you name, and deletes them in descending index order so each index stays valid. A named track that holds a clip refuses the whole batch rather than being skipped silently, a Set that would be left with no tracks is refused, and an apply without confirm: true writes nothing. Irreversible on this build, so a dry run only lists what would go.

tracks.description: Exact track names to check; omit to scan every track.

confirm.description: Must be true to apply; this cannot be undone.

tools.name: mix_routing_report
tools.summary: Every track's input and output routing, with unreadable rows flagged.
tools.description: Reads input and output type and channel live, in Live's own display names with Live's identifiers beside them, the current option's index where it can be matched, and how many options each track offers. A nameless channel reports its index instead of an object repr. Routing is read here rather than in the snapshot so a plain read does not pay for it. A track whose routing cannot be read carries the reason in its row and is listed in flagged; an empty output is flagged too, never reported as a clean route. A nameless channel with zero selectable options is not flagged, because there is no choice to resolve.

tools.name: library_folders
tools.summary: List the browser's top-level categories and their child counts.
tools.description: Reads Live's browser categories — sounds, drums, instruments, effects, samples, packs, user library and the rest — with each one's display name, URI and child count. A category this build does not expose is listed in missing with the reason instead of being omitted silently. Read-only: nothing is loaded.

tools.name: library_browse
tools.summary: Page one browser folder's children by path.
tools.description: Walks the browser tree from a category by exact folder name, for example 'user_library' or 'sounds/Bass', and returns one page of children with name, folder flag, loadable flag and URI. A missing or ambiguous step is an error naming it; an unreadable folder reports the reason. Read-only and paged, because a sample category can hold thousands of items.

tools.name: devices_set_parameter
tools.summary: Set one device parameter by name or index, with an exact undo token.
tools.description: Resolves one track, one device on it and one parameter, each strictly by exact name or by index. A device name matching several devices is refused with the candidate indexes instead of picking the first, because two EQ Eights on one chain is normal. The value must sit inside the parameter's own min and max, and a disabled parameter is refused before Live sees the write. The change reports the value before and Live's read-back after, and the undo token restores the exact prior number.
examples: turn the EQ gain down 3 dB
set the compressor threshold on the drum bus
close the filter on the bass

track.description: Exact track name; duplicates are rejected.

device.description: Exact device name on that track.

parameter.description: Exact parameter name, for example Gain.

value.description: The new value, inside the parameter's own range.

tools.name: devices_set_macro
tools.summary: Set a rack macro by number, with the same undo token as a parameter write.
tools.description: A rack exposes Macro 1 to Macro 16 at parameter indexes 1 to 16, right after Device On, and Live reports whatever name the user gave each macro; the first real rack checked had Low Gain, Mid Gain, High Gain and Vintage on macros 1 to 4. The macro therefore resolves by position, so a renamed macro still responds to its number, and the row reports the name actually found. Only racks carry macros, so a bare EQ Eight is refused with a reason rather than guessed at. Give exactly one of value or fraction: value is in the macro's native units, which on a real rack was a 0..127-style range rather than 0..1, while fraction takes 0..1 of that range and maps it. The undo token restores the prior number.
examples: set macro 1 on the rack to half
open the filter macro a little

track.description: Exact track name; duplicates are rejected.

device.description: Exact rack name on that track.

value.description: The new value in the macro's native units, e.g. 63.5 on a 0..127 macro.

fraction.description: The new value as 0..1 of the macro's range; give this instead of value.

tools.name: devices_move
tools.summary: Reorder one device within its chain, with an exact undo token.
tools.description: Moves the resolved device to a final index in the same track's chain and reads the chain back to confirm the device landed there. It uses Track.move_device where this build exposes it and Song.move_device(device, track, position) where only the song-level mover exists, which is the case on 12.2.5. The undo token moves it back from where it ended up, so a restore is exact rather than positional guesswork. The chain length must be unchanged; a backend that loses or duplicates devices during the move is reported as a Live error.
examples: put the compressor before the EQ
move the saturation to the end of the chain

track.description: Exact track name; duplicates are rejected.

tools.name: devices_delete
tools.summary: Delete one device from a chain; irreversible on this Live build, so it needs confirm.
tools.description: Deletes the resolved device and checks the chain shrank by exactly one. This build cannot put a device back: insert_device arrives in Live 12.3, so the delete has no undo token and is declared irreversible. An apply therefore refuses without confirm: true, while a dry run previews the device and states that confirmation is required.
examples: remove the broken plug-in from this chain

track.description: Exact track name; duplicates are rejected.

confirm.description: Must be true to apply; this cannot be undone.

tools.name: devices_browse_presets
tools.summary: List device preset folders, or one device's presets, from the browser.
tools.description: Reads the instruments, audio-effects and MIDI-effects categories. Without a device it lists the preset folders with child counts; with an exact device name it lists that folder's presets and their URIs. It never loads anything. Every folder is read before the page is sliced, so a paging count is real and a named device is found wherever it sits in the tree, whatever Live reports for is_folder, and a name that exists in two categories is refused rather than guessed; a category that cannot be read reports the reason, and only a scan past 2000 folders is reported as stopped.
examples: what presets do I have for EQ Eight
which instrument folders are in my library

device.description: Exact preset-folder name, e.g. EQ Eight.

tools.name: devices_read_parameters
tools.summary: List a device's parameters with the exact names, values and ranges a write needs.
tools.description: Reads one device's parameter vector from Live, one page at a time. Every row carries the exact name devices_set_parameter takes, the current value in Live's own units, its display string, its min and max, whether Live quantises it, and whether it is enabled. This is the read that makes a parameter write usable: without it, finding Stereo Width means probing indexes. The device resolves by exact name or index, and a duplicate device name is refused with the candidate indexes rather than guessed.
examples: what parameters does this compressor have
what is the EQ gain called on this device

track.description: Exact track name; duplicates are rejected.

device.description: Exact device name on that track.

tools.name: master_set_gain
tools.summary: Set the master fader, with the exact prior value as an undo token.
tools.description: Writes song.master_track.mixer_device.volume, the fader the snapshot does not carry and mix_levels_report therefore reports as unmeasured. The value is normalised 0..1 like a track fader and must sit inside the fader's own range. A dry run reports the current value, the target and both display strings without writing; the undo token restores the exact prior number. A Live build with no master track reports unsupported with the reason rather than pretending the write happened.

value.description: The new fader value, normally 0 to 1.

tools.name: mix_snapshot_save
tools.summary: Capture the whole balance as a file the Set does not have to change for.
tools.description: Captures every track and return's volume, pan, sends, mute and solo, plus the master fader the snapshot cannot see, into a small JSON snapshot stored beside the plans. The Set is not written at all. The response names the snapshot id, the file, the per-track rows and any field that could not be read, so a snapshot is never silently partial. Save one before a risky mix move and restore it exactly afterwards.
examples: snapshot this balance before I change it

tools.name: mix_snapshot_restore
tools.summary: Put a saved mix back, refusing a Set that no longer matches it.
tools.description: Applies a snapshot from mix_snapshot_save, or the undo token from an earlier restore, field by field across tracks, returns and the master fader. Dry-run by default and reports every change with both display strings and the exact prior values as an undo token. It refuses with nothing written when the Set no longer matches the snapshot's track names at the same indexes, so a reordered Set cannot move the wrong fader. A write that Live refuses reverts the fields this call already changed before raising, so a failed restore never leaves half a mix behind.

snapshot_id.description: A snapshot id from mix_snapshot_save, like m_0123abcd.

restore.description: An undo token from an earlier restore.
